title: Wishful Thinking
year_note: The parent album came out on 31 October 1983 and the single in December 1983 (Wikipedia's song page and other sources give early January 1984); it peaked in January 1984. 1983 is the original release year.
album: Working with Fire and Steel – Possible Pop Songs Volume Two

notes.made: Gary Daly and Eddie Lundon wrote it after a weekend away trying to write a country song in the style of Brian Eno's 'Here He Comes'. Mike Howlett produced the album at Amazon Studios in Liverpool and The Manor in Oxfordshire, bringing in an E-mu Emulator next to real horns, woodwind and strings. Lundon, who wrote the words, sings lead, not Daly. Steve Levy plays the oboe.
notes.context: China Crisis came from Kirkby on the edge of Liverpool, working-class lads who met at a Catholic boys' school and loved Steely Dan, Bowie and Eno. They premiered the song on a John Peel session in January 1983, when it seemed like an album track. Released as the third single, it went to 9 in early 1984, their only UK top ten, and topped Sweden's Poporama radio chart that March. Walter Becker of Steely Dan produced their next album.

listen_for.note: That is Eddie Lundon's voice, not the usual Gary Daly, which is part of why it sounds lighter than the rest of their records.
Steve Levy's oboe (he plays it on tracks 5 to 7 of the album, and this is track 6), the instrument Trouser Press singled out as the band's surprise.
The Emulator sampler Howlett introduced; one review called it an 'Emulator laced' single.

leads_to.title: Here He Comes
leads_to.why: The song they were trying to imitate, from Before and After Science, which Eno co-produced with Rhett Davies, later the producer of Avalon.

notes.unverified: Tomasz's quote is wrong on the singer: Eddie Lundon sings lead on this one, not Gary Daly (Wikipedia and electricityclub.co.uk). His UK number 9 is right. Gary Johnson plays fretless bass on the album, but I couldn't confirm it on this track.

culture.title: UK number 9
culture.line: Their only UK top ten, peaking in January 1984. It was a top 20 hit in several European countries and number one on Sweden's Poporama radio chart on 8 March 1984.

culture.title: First heard on Peel
culture.line: China Crisis premiered it on a BBC John Peel session in January 1983, with the Waterboys' drummer Kevin Wilkinson sitting in.

culture.title: Fortieth anniversary tour
culture.line: In autumn 2023 the band played the whole of Working with Fire and Steel live across the UK.
